consequence.statement: Existing UpdateRequest objects stay stored as v1beta1 until rewritten; the operator must run a storage version migration (re-write all objects) and update status.storedVersions before a later release removes v1beta1.
consequence.remediation: After upgrading, run a storage version migration for updaterequests.kyverno.io (re-write all UpdateRequest objects at the new storage version) and update the CRD's status.storedVersions before upgrading to a release that removes v1beta1.

original.statement: The storage version of the updaterequests.kyverno.io CRD changed from v1beta1 to v2 (v1beta1.storage true→false, v2.storage false→true between 1.12.6 and 1.13.0), so existing UpdateRequest objects stay stored as v1beta1 until rewritten and a storage version migration plus a status.storedVersions update is required before a later release removes v1beta1.

consequence.statement: New or rewritten UpdateRequest objects are stored as v2, while existing objects stay stored as v1beta1 until rewritten. v1beta1 is still served, so nothing stops working in this release.
consequence.remediation: Optional: rewrite existing UpdateRequest objects so they are stored as v2, and check the CRD's status.storedVersions. Do this before any future release that removes v1beta1.

corrected.statement: From 1.12.6 to 1.13.0 the storage version of updaterequests.kyverno.io changes from v1beta1 to v2. v1beta1 is still served, so existing UpdateRequest objects keep working and stay stored as v1beta1 until rewritten. No breakage or mandatory step is stated for this release.

decision.reason: [ev-cf5b10ff8047] and [ev-d3850c78b94e] only show the storage flag moving from v1beta1 to v2 between 1.12.6 and 1.13.0. The CRD validator confirms v1beta1 is still served in both releases, so existing objects keep working. No upstream excerpt says anything fails, that a step is mandatory for this upgrade, or that v1beta1 is deprecated or scheduled for removal; the migration advice comes only from the diff tool's generated text and depends on a hypothetical later removal. The consequence is therefore behavior-change (review), not migration-required.
